title: The Front-Loaded Mortgage Shock

beats.say: You sign a 30-year mortgage for $400,000 at 6.5%.
beats.visual: A person holding a fountain pen over thick white paper on a dark wooden desk, close-up on hands only, moody cinematic lighting.

beats.say: You think your monthly payment splits evenly between the loan and the bank's fee.
beats.visual: A sleek silver calculator resting on a minimalist marble kitchen counter, natural side light casting long shadows.

beats.say: It doesn't. Here's the brutal math they hide from you.
beats.visual: An empty modern hallway with concrete walls, illuminated by a single overhead pendant light, dramatic perspective lines.

beats.say: After 5 full years of making on-time payments, you've handed over roughly $150,000.
beats.visual: A stack of thick manila envelopes resting on a dark slate table, shot from a high angle with shallow depth of field.

beats.say: You assume a massive chunk of that cash now belongs to you.
beats.visual: A close-up of a brass door key resting on a rustic oak tabletop, soft ambient evening light.

beats.say: You'd be wrong. But here's the part nobody mentions.
beats.visual: A glowing digital clock on a bedside table showing late night hours, blurred background in deep shadow.

beats.say: Out of that $150,000, only $17,000 actually paid down the principal balance.
beats.visual: A digital screen showing a steep downward red line on a dark grid, shot from behind at a sharp angle.

beats.say: The remaining $133,000 vanished straight into bank interest and escrow fees.
beats.visual: A brass vault door slightly ajar in a dimly lit concrete room, heavy shadows, cold industrial aesthetic.

beats.say: Banks front-load your amortization schedule so they collect their profits first.
beats.visual: A tall glass hourglass with black sand draining rapidly into the bottom bulb, macro lens, dark background.

beats.say: For the first decade, you are basically renting your own home from the lender.
beats.visual: A large suburban house seen from the street at dusk, warm interior lights glowing behind drawn blinds.

beats.say: Know the math before you sign the contract.
beats.visual: A clean wooden desk with a black coffee mug and a blank leather notebook, top-down minimalist composition.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A person walking away down a long concrete sidewalk at sunset, long silhouette, calm cinematic mood.

caption: The brutal math behind a 30-year mortgage that banks never explain. #mortgageloan #personalfinance #moneytips #financialliteracy #debtfree
description: An analysis of a $400,000 mortgage at 6.5% reveals how front-loaded interest steals your equity in the first five years.
first_comment: Did you know how little principal you actually pay in the first five years?

facts.claim: A 30-year mortgage of $400,000 at 6.5% front-loads interest so that after 5 years and roughly $150,000 in total payments, only about $17,000 goes to principal.
facts.basis: Standard loan amortization math for a $400,000 loan at 6.5% interest over 30 years (monthly payment approx $2,528; total 5-year payments approx $151,680, principal paid approx $17,450).
